title: Ada and the Will
premise: Estate lawyer Cyrus Nakamura is summoned to execute the will of Marisol Vance, a woman who vanished seven years ago and was declared dead without a body. The will's existence is impossible—dated after her disappearance—and it names Cyrus, the man who quietly filed away every uncomfortable truth about the town of Greywater Cove. As Cyrus reads Marisol's recovered diary, whose entries continue past the date she disappeared, they realize someone has been writing in her voice for years to keep an investigation buried. With the help of Marisol's estranged half-sister Junie and a retired harbor master who owes Marisol his life, Cyrus sets a trap using the will itself as bait, forcing the killer—a beloved town patriarch who drowned Marisol to protect a smuggling operation—to confess before the spring tide exposes her remains. In the end, Cyrus chooses truth over the town's fragile peace, loses their law practice, but gains a found family in Junie and the harbor community.
about_author: Emrys Thornbury is the pen name of a former small-town paralegal who spent a decade watching secrets move through probate files. They write coastal mysteries about people who mistake silence for safety.

chapters.title: The Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Cyrus Nakamura's POV. A courier delivers a sealed will for Marisol Vance—dated eleven months after her disappearance. Cyrus, who probated her presumed-death order years ago, recognizes the impossible date and feels seven years of careful invisibility begin to crack. Emotional beat: dread disguised as professional curiosity.

chapters.title: Greywater Cove Keeps Its Ledgers
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Flashback-woven chapter establishing how Cyrus became the town's keeper of inconvenient documents, including the file on Marisol's case that was quietly thinned by someone with authority. Emotional beat: complicity—the ache of having survived by staying useful to powerful people.

chapters.title: The Diary Arrives by Tide
chapters.summary: Junie Vance's POV. Marisol's half-sister Junie finds the diary wedged in a lobster trap, its final entries dated months after the disappearance—in handwriting that falters but continues. She brings it to Cyrus because he's the only name in the will. Emotional beat: grief reignited into suspicion.

chapters.title: Entries After the End
chapters.summary: Alternating Cyrus/Junie POV. Reading the post-disappearance entries aloud, they notice the diary describes events only insiders would know—including a reference to 'the lawyer who alphabetizes my absence.' Someone wrote these pages to steer whoever finally read them. Emotional beat: vertigo; the past is being actively maintained.

chapters.title: Executor of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The will leaves everything to Junie but conditions it on 'the tide giving back what it took'—a phrase Cyrus traces to the harbor master, Elias Boone. First interview with Elias reveals he pulled Marisol's boat from the water the night she vanished and never told police. Emotional beat: the first real ally, and the first real risk.

chapters.title: The Man Who Files Better Than Police
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus reconstructs the original case file from memory and private copies, discovering pages were removed by Judge Aldous Wren—town patriarch, smuggling-era power broker, and the man who signed Marisol's death declaration. Emotional beat: cold clarity about who benefits from Marisol staying missing.

chapters.title: Junie Comes Home
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. Junie moves into Marisol's shuttered house against the town's quiet disapproval, finding signs someone has been entering it for years—fresh oil on hinges, a kettle moved. Emotional beat: defiant belonging; claiming a home everyone wants empty.

chapters.title: What the Smugglers Buried
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias recounts the cove's smuggling history and the night Marisol confronted Wren about a shipment gone wrong, threatening to go to the coast guard. He admits he helped load her boat that night, believing she was leaving town voluntarily. Emotional beat: guilt as loyalty weaponized—he protected the wrong secret out of love.

chapters.title: A Visitor in the Night
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Someone ransacks Cyrus's office, taking the diary copy but leaving the original will—too public to steal. A note in Marisol's handwriting warns Cyrus to stop reading. The killer knows the case file intimately, better than investigators did. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Handwriting Test
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus compares diary entries across years and identifies three distinct hands: Marisol's early entries, a skilled imitator's later ones, and a third hand copying the imitator—someone practicing. The forgery was rehearsed, which means time, access, and motive. Emotional beat: the hunter realizing the prey is also hunting.

chapters.title: Wren's Hospitality
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. Junie accepts dinner at the Wren estate, playing the grateful heir while cataloguing a locked boathouse and a framed photo of the cove from the night Marisol vanished—Wren in it, dry, though he claimed to be inland. Emotional beat: performance as armor; found-family bonds forming between Junie and Cyrus over shared deception.

chapters.title: The Second Diary
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Following a detail from the forged entries, Cyrus finds a second notebook hidden in the probate archive—a surveillance record Wren kept on Marisol, logging her movements until the night she died. The last entry reads simply: 'Tide's right.' Emotional beat: horror transmuted into evidence.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Invoice
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Wren confronts Elias, invoking the debt of the smuggling years, demanding he silence Cyrus. Elias refuses, choosing Marisol's memory over forty years of obligation. Emotional beat: the theme crystallized—loyalty vs. truth, and what survival actually cost him.

chapters.title: Fire at the Archive
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The county records annex burns overnight; the original disappearance file is destroyed. Cyrus's off-site copies survive, but the arson confirms Wren is moving from concealment to elimination. Emotional beat: escalation—the town's machinery of silence now openly violent.

chapters.title: The Trap Is Baited
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus drafts a fake codicil announcing that Marisol's remains have been located offshore and that the will's full terms—including a sealed confession she recorded—will be read at the spring tide. It's fiction, but it forces the killer to act where Cyrus controls the ground. Emotional beat: the invisible man stepping into the light on purpose.

chapters.title: Junie in the Crosshairs
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. Wren offers Junie a settlement to contest the will and leave town; when she refuses, he threatens her with her sister's fate. Junie records the conversation. Emotional beat: terror braided with fury—she refuses to be a second missing Vance.

chapters.title: Spring Tide
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. At the tide reading, staged on the harbor with Elias, Junie, and a state investigator Cyrus secretly briefed, Cyrus reads the fabricated codicil aloud. Wren, certain the 'confession recording' exists, moves to destroy it—and walks directly into the trap. Emotional beat: controlled tension snapping toward release.

chapters.title: The Confession He Thinks Is His Own
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Confronted with the surveillance notebook, the handwriting analysis, and witnesses, Wren unravels and confesses: he drowned Marisol when she refused to stay bought, then spent seven years forging her diary to control any future investigation. Elias's corroboration seals it. Emotional beat: catharsis with a bitter aftertaste—justice arriving too late to be clean.

chapters.title: What the Tide Gives Back
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. Divers guided by Elias recover Marisol's remains beneath the wreck of her own boat. Junie finally buries her sister, reading the true last entry—the one in Marisol's real hand, asking Junie not to let the town decide what happened to her. Emotional beat: grief given somewhere to go.

chapters.title: Probate of a Town
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Wren's empire collapses into indictments; the bar association suspends Cyrus for the fabricated codicil despite the outcome. Cyrus, unexpectedly unafraid, realizes invisibility was never safety—only a slower drowning. Emotional beat: loss accepted as the price of truth.

chapters.title: The House Stays in the Family
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. Junie reopens Marisol's house as a harbor archive where the town's suppressed records—smuggling ledgers, missing-persons files—are preserved publicly. Elias donates his logs; former townsfolk bring boxes of things they were told to forget. Emotional beat: found family becoming something structural, not just personal.

chapters.title: Alphabetized No More
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV, closing. Cyrus, working unofficially from the archive, files the last page of the true diary under Marisol's own name instead of a case number. Walking the tideline at dawn, Cyrus reflects that some wills are executed by lawyers, and some by the living. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace—the survivor finally surfacing.
